name: Mark Takano

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AFFORDABLE HEALTHCARE
statements.title: AFFORDABLE HEALTHCARE
sentences: First of all, the Republicans started a war of choice, not of necessity, a war of choice in Iran costing taxpayers roughly $40 billion so far, and increased inflation by at least 2.3 percent.
They passed that bill last year, which gave to the rich by taking from the middle class and from the people who are in poverty.
Monthly premiums for ACA plans rose by over 97 percent in California in 2026 and rose by 99 percent in my district, which is almost 100 percent.
More than 4 out of 10 ACA enrollees said higher insurance costs have made it harder for them to afford other basics in life besides health insurance.
By the end of this year, an average of 17.5 million people will lose their ACA coverage.
A key tenet of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which I said was ironically named, was so-called work requirements for Medicaid.
Let's call these work requirements what they really are: paperwork requirements that were created to make it impossible for American families to access the healthcare that they need.
These paperwork requirements are for the hundreds of thousands of people living with HIV who rely on Medicaid to receive treatment.

It is about trying to squeeze as many people off of healthcare and health insurance as possible, so that more dollars can be shifted and transferred to the wealthiest and richest corporations in our country.
When parents lose access to Medicaid, their children often fall off the healthcare rolls, as well.
I will fight the Trump agenda and work with my colleagues to repeal the inhumane Medicaid paperwork requirements, which only serve as a barrier to healthcare.
I will fight for the subsidies that made the ACA healthcare plans more accessible to millions of Americans.
I will fight for bills like my PrEP Access and Coverage Act, which will expand access to healthcare and ensure more people receive lifesaving treatments.
I will fight to make sure that our schools are funded and that our students have the resources they need to grow, learn, and succeed.
I will fight to make life more affordable for everyday Americans and to ensure that everyone has access to the American Dream.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2102, MAJOR RICHARD STAR ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2102, MAJOR RICHARD STAR ACT
sentences: That is a value proposition that I simply cannot understand, let alone support, especially not when we have no problem whatsoever running up debt to send these very same veterans to war in the first place.
We will honor this institution and the veterans who have defended it by being forthright, open, and truthful.
We have before us a very worthy bill, the Major Richard Star Act, which I strongly support.
So I urge my colleagues to support this bill, as I will, without hesitation.
Mr. Speaker, I strongly urge my colleagues to support this legislation.
Let us show our veterans and the American people that we mean what we say here in Congress when we pledge to support our Nation's veterans.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2102, MAJOR RICHARD STAR ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2102, MAJOR RICHARD STAR ACT
sentences: I will add that the current Republican majority has no problem absorbing the cost of tax breaks for billionaires, also in the neighborhood of a trillion dollars.
No more handwringing and disingenuous talk of debt and deficits, and no more hiding behind hollow words of support without meaningful action to back them up.
Earlier this week, we voted on the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of- Living Adjustment Act, which would raise the level of disability compensation to match inflation.
So those servicemembers President Trump keeps sending into harm's way in this foolish and reckless war with Iran would be ineligible for these benefits.
We have heard the kind of self-righteous indignation on debt and deficit for decades from Republicans.
All the while, they run up the tab on Pentagon spending and tax cuts for the wealthy.
The question is on adoption of the resolution.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of this rule, which would finally allow us to consider H.R. 2102, otherwise known as the Major Richard Star Act.

Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues in the strongest possible terms to support our wounded warriors, honor the promise we made to them, support the Major Richard Star Act, and vote ``yes'' on this rule.
I believe tomorrow we are going to get it done.

Yes, there are many good aspects to H.R. 9237 for veterans, survivors, and caregivers, as well, but as long as those good things are paid for by cutting benefits for other current or future veterans, I cannot support it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS BENEFITS
statements.title: VETERANS BENEFITS
sentences: September is Suicide Prevention Month.
Suicide Prevention Month is a perfect time to bring attention to this critical issue and to show support for veterans who need it.
Unfortunately, my Republican colleagues declined to hold a single suicide prevention hearing in the month of September last year, and, sadly, no hearings were planned for this year.
Right now, veterans are struggling to access their care and benefits, including mental health care.
Too many veterans are facing the affordability crisis, which is leading to spikes in homelessness and home foreclosures.
For my Republican colleagues to try and rip veterans' benefits away now, while we are in an active conflict with Iran, is a slap in the face to every servicemember in harm's way.

VA is also giving American taxpayers the opportunity to line the pockets of healthcare conglomerates, like UnitedHealthcare and private equity giants, with the VA's new community care contracts, amounting to $1 trillion.
Just months into the 119th Congress, Chairman Van Orden and Chairman Bost urged President Trump and Secretary Collins to end the most important foreclosure relief program for veterans.
The VA informed the committee that the decision sent over 15,000 veterans and their families into foreclosure and tens of thousands more at risk of losing their homes.
Our own estimates now put that figure in excess of 17,000 foreclosures.
President Biden, with the support of Congress, used existing authorities to pause foreclosures that were occurring during the pandemic.
That is what this chart shows, the plummeting number of foreclosures.
This resulted in VA losing authorities to continue foreclosure mitigation.
President Biden instituted a second foreclosure moratorium to give VA time to offer a solution.
Look at what happens to foreclosures when they implement and address the issue, following through on the pandemic.
Most lenders worked with the Biden administration to ensure that very few veteran foreclosures occurred.
According to VA's own data from June, this has led to over 15,000 veteran foreclosures.
At the beginning of this Congress, both Chairman Bost and Economic Subcommittee Chairman Van Orden announced ending veteran homelessness as one of their top priorities.
Yet, there has not been a single piece of legislation related to veteran homelessness brought to the House floor, nor a subcommittee hearing on the topic.
In fact, the policies that Chairman Bost and Congressman Van Orden advocated actually produced more housing insecurity among veterans by ending VA home loan foreclosure protections.
I have asked repeatedly how VA has helped these families who are facing foreclosure, but the Trump VA has refused to provide that information.
The VA has refused to tell me how many of these families became at risk of homelessness due to their home foreclosure.

I remain committed to leading the fight to end veteran homelessness and creating a housing ecosystem that serves the needs of everyone, instead of prioritizing profits and the bottom line of billionaires.
I will take this opportunity to say to any veterans watching: You are not alone and support is available.
For example, last night, the discharge petition Representative Raul Ruiz and I introduced on the Major Richard Star Act received the 218th signature to force a vote in the House.

Subpoenas effectively die and lack enforcement power when the 119th Congress ends, but I can assure Oracle and the public that my Democratic colleagues and I will not back down from our demands for transparency and accountability.
But my Democratic colleagues and I will not quit asking the hard questions and pushing VA to use its resources to help vulnerable families.
I will continue to push back on needless policies that create housing insecurity for veteran families.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027
statements.title: NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027
sentences: Madam Chair, this amendment would codify President Trump's executive order banning transgender Americans from serving in the United States military.
There is no evidence that having transgender troops negatively impacts military readiness.
Once again, my Republican colleagues are moving forward with a sweeping ban on necessary healthcare, including mental health care for children.
This amendment will force servicemembers out of the military either for their own sake or for the sake of their children since this amendment bans mental health care for trans children.
What parent would choose staying in their job if that means denying their child access to mental health care?
Madam Chair, I rise in opposition to this amendment.
Madam Chair, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on this amendment.
Mr. Chair, I rise in opposition to this amendment.
This is an inhumane, wasteful, regressive amendment, and I urge my colleagues to vote ``no.'' Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to this amendment.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TAKE CARE OF AMERICA'S VETERANS ACT
statements.title: TAKE CARE OF AMERICA'S VETERANS ACT
sentences: In addition to the numerous VSOs and over two dozen labor unions opposed to this bill, including the Union of Veterans Council, American Federation of Government Employees, and AFL-CIO, so do professional associations like the American Psychological Association and the Nurses Organization of VA.
The majority has decided that, during a housing affordability crisis, it makes sense to raise costs on struggling veteran homeowners who are desperately trying to avoid foreclosure.

It would accelerate the privatization of veteran healthcare--creating new grant programs for private providers that divert resources from VA mental health and PTSD programs--and steer veterans into more expensive community-based care, even where VA services remain available, and strip VA psychologists of their collective bargaining rights.

There is $1.5 trillion for the Department of Defense, $70 billion for the Department of Homeland Security, and hundreds of millions of dollars for permanent tax cuts for the wealthy, none of it offset, and all of which the chairman voted for enthusiastically.
Just 10 days of President Trump's folly in Iran would pay for 10 years of benefits under the Major Richard Star Act.
Those servicemembers President Trump keeps sending into harm's way in this foolish war with Iran would be ineligible for these benefits.

Let me just say a ``yes'' vote on this bill is a message that we are sending to the servicemembers currently serving in and around the waters of Iran and the Strait of Hormuz and our servicemembers that are stationed at bases who have already faced incoming missile fire and have been subjected to the blasts that have surely affected their eardrums, we are saying to them that they will not be able to apply to make claims based on tinnitus, much less sleep apnea.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to H.R. 9237.
Mr. Speaker, I reject that premise, I reject this bill, and I encourage others to do the same.
Mr. Speaker, for those reasons and many, many more, I cannot in good conscience support this legislation.
We are going to hear arguments from the majority today about all the good things this bill attempts to do.
Regrettably, we will also hear the chairman say that cutting veterans' benefits is the only way that we can get them done.
I will point to this chart here.
We do not support the Take Care of America's Veterans Act, H.R. 9237, and we will never elect Representatives who want to cut veterans' benefits.
I am not going to let them do that.

For that reason, we do not support the funding mechanism within the Take Care of America's Veterans Act (H.R. 9237/S. 4744) that would significantly reduce future benefits for more than a million disabled veterans.
We continue to support enactment of a clean and complete Major Richard Star Act that delivers full concurrent receipt to combat-injured retirees without reducing earned benefits for future veterans.
We fully support the original MAJ Richard Star act, but can not abide by taking from one group of veterans to pay another.
We will be watching your vote on this carefully.

He is making a claim, but, again, I will contend that they are counting on a golden egg in disability cuts, savings on the backs of veterans, that has not been laid yet and that I contend will not be.

I will point out that yesterday, House Republicans released a $95 billion supplemental for the reconciliation bill they want to bring forward next week for Pentagon spending, farm assistance, and intelligence operations all without offsets.
Yet, we are asking our veterans to pay for this bill.
Before my colleagues say I have cherry-picked those comments, I urge them to pull out their phones and take a look at the comment sections on any social media post discussing this bill.
If my colleagues won't listen to my concerns here, I urge them to listen to the veterans, dependents, caregivers, survivors, and advocates in their districts.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FIGHTING BACK AGAINST DISMANTLING OF VOTING RIGHTS
statements.title: FIGHTING BACK AGAINST DISMANTLING OF VOTING RIGHTS
sentences: Bloody Sunday, you will recall, is that moment in Selma when John Lewis, among others, crossed the Edmund Pettus Bridge and were met with State troopers and the local police and they were bludgeoned and whipped and were charged by officers on horseback because they were marching to Montgomery to demand voting rights.
He said: ``The most basic right of all was the right to choose your own leaders.'' A few months after that speech, the Voting Rights Act was the law of the land.
The Supreme Court has taken a wrecking ball to that progress in its decision in Louisiana v. Callais.

I know that while the Supreme Court may have dismantled the Voting Rights Act, Congress is not powerless, and the American people, in spite of the efforts to rig the maps and to draw districts to keep Republicans in power, we can and will prevail in the coming months.
There is no question that this Supreme Court is facing a crisis of credibility.
Mr. Speaker, it is also time to put a check on the Supreme Court, the Supreme Court that has taken a wrecking ball to the Voting Rights Act.
I won't claim to be the first Japanese American in Congress.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS 2ND AMENDMENT PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: VETERANS 2ND AMENDMENT PROTECTION ACT
sentences: May is Mental Health Awareness Month, and it also happens to be Military Appreciation Month.
It goes without saying that there is a mental health crisis in this country.
Americans of all stripes lack access to the resources necessary to properly care for their mental health--or fail to fully realize them--and they suffer because of this crisis.
Veterans are certainly no exception, and they face additional challenges due to service-connected mental health conditions.
Many veterans can access mental health care through the VA, but those not connected to VA care may face additional challenges seeking resources and support.
Unfortunately, because of cheap, easy access to firearms in this country, our Nation's mental health crisis is one of the many contributors to the epidemic of suicide and gun violence in America.
This bill is not about the Second Amendment.
The majority is using the Second Amendment as branding for a bill that has nothing to do with veterans losing rights for seeking care.
More specifically, Republicans desire to invoke the sacred Second Amendment and use the issue of access to firearms for political gain, and that is what is driving this conversation.
What we will hear from Republicans is that fear of having their Second Amendment rights encroached upon leads to a reluctance of veterans to seek mental health care.
Under no circumstances does seeking mental health care at the VA lead to a loss of rights or firearms, and if the Republicans were interested in the truth, they would acknowledge that.

We are going to hear from Republicans that the VA's decision to assign someone a fiduciary and subsequently add their name to the NICS list is based on whether someone can balance their checkbook or whether they can manage their benefits.
Mr. Speaker, at times I feel like we are screaming into the void regarding gun violence.
It is about recycling a decade-old talking point, stoking fear about VA care, and hiding behind the Second Amendment because they do not have a serious governing agenda.

There is very limited information publicly available about the population of veterans deemed to be financially incompetent who have historically been reported to the NICS list and whether they, on average, have elevated rates of suicidality or violence.
We have no data on if fear of losing Second Amendment rights is a major impediment to seeking help or if other factors are more important.
In other words, the claim that fear of losing Second Amendment rights is a major impediment to seeking help is a claim being made that has not been borne out by any sort of research or study.
We also don't know the long-term mental health outcomes of those in the fiduciary program.

What Republicans have put forth here today is a philosophical debate about the absoluteness of the Second Amendment, and they have made this argument in the absence of data to push legislation without safeguards that will have real-life consequences.
Veterans are not having their weapons taken away if they utilize VA mental health care.
I would encourage my colleagues to stop intentionally spreading misinformation.
The Veterans Health Administration, where veterans would be receiving care, has absolutely no role in this process and absolutely no communication with the Department of Justice or the NICS list.
A veteran can appeal the assignment of a fiduciary and their subsequent reporting to NICS both before and after the fact, including in Federal court.
Mr. Speaker, I yield 2 minutes to the gentlewoman from the great State of Georgia (Mrs. McBath), who is my good friend and a passionate advocate for gun safety in America.
As the chairman said, this is not about gun rights.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to this bill and I urge my colleagues to vote against it, as well.
I will note, though, that VA data indicates that not many people choose to appeal this decision.

If it wasn't already clear that my colleagues are only here to put on a show, I will remind everyone that even if this bill were to be signed into law today, it would have no effect whatsoever on the processes and procedures at VA.
For those reasons and many more, I strongly oppose this bill, and I urge my colleagues to vote against it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SMITHSONIAN AMERICAN WOMEN'S HISTORY MUSEUM ACT
statements.title: SMITHSONIAN AMERICAN WOMEN'S HISTORY MUSEUM ACT

Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to reject this bill and pass the original bipartisan bill with the National Museum of the American Latino.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SHARRI BRILEY AND ERIC EDMUNDSON VETERANS BENEFITS EXPANSION ACT OF 2026
statements.title: SHARRI BRILEY AND ERIC EDMUNDSON VETERANS BENEFITS EXPANSION ACT OF 2026
sentences: At a time when we are spending trillions on defense, trillions on tax cuts for the wealthy, and countless other frivolities, like ballrooms and a slush fund for the President's friends, to suggest that we can only help veterans by hurting them is patently ridiculous.
I want to clearly state that we owe our servicemembers, veterans, their families, and their survivors a debt of gratitude, as they have given everything to this Nation.
Chairman Bost and Representative Van Orden cheered on this development as thousands of veterans suddenly faced tenuous financial circumstances and no resources to turn to as they faced foreclosure.
Let me say, in the past 12 months since the closure of the VASP program, 10,000 veterans have lost their homes due to foreclosure.
We could call this the Secretary Collins, Representative Van Orden, and Chairman Bost foreclosure program.
What we are seeing today is an attempt to take away affordable housing for veterans.
Even more critical, these are veterans attempting to keep their homes amidst rapidly rising foreclosures.

We certainly didn't have this debate when we were offsetting a $30 billion war of choice in Iran, which will only make more veterans, Trump's $1 billion new ballroom, or a $75 billion slush fund for ICE, which now the Senate is having trouble getting over to the House.
If my counterparts in the Republican Party truly gave a damn about veterans, they would not pit them against one another just to give them a meager downpayment on veteran benefits.
They are silent on the subject of should you ask our servicemembers who are serving right now in the waters around Iran whether they should be charged $1,000 or more in fees to refinance their homes.
Many more veterans are facing foreclosure.
We are also looking at potentially a $1.5 trillion defense budget increase, and there is talk about $1 billion on the President's ballroom.
I had an amendment that would have delayed for 3 years the implementation of a big, bad, ugly bill tax break we were giving to very wealthy people--people with $15 million to pass on to their heirs.
It is not too much to ask the wealthiest people of our country to bear the cost of paying for the catastrophically disabled veterans.

I think the American people would countenance that much better than: Let's take away the ability for our servicemembers who are currently serving in the waters surrounding Iran, or our veterans--we shouldn't be asking them to have to pay more in home loan fees for benefits that they thought they were getting when they signed up.
Veterans are experiencing record foreclosures.
The VASP program was a lifeline offered to veterans by President Biden that served as a last resort option for veterans before foreclosure.
It is no surprise that foreclosures for veterans have doubled since that action.

In fact, if you want to continue to increase funding for defense spending and military aid, I would say that you should be required to consider the long-term cost of taking care of the servicemembers whom we are sending into harm's way.
That is why I oppose this bill.
Now, we are asking veterans to shoulder the cost of survivors and catastrophically injured veterans--again, taking from one set of veterans in order to help another group of very deserving veterans.
Again, I will emphasize the impossible position we are putting our veteran community in.
We cannot allow ourselves to accept veterans paying for their own benefits, and we should not tolerate forcing this community to fight each other in a pecking order of who matters most.
That is why I simply cannot support this legislation as written, and I encourage my colleagues to do the same.
Meanwhile, we will see more veterans foreclosed upon.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PARENTAL RIGHTS OVER THE EDUCATION AND CARE OF THEIR KIDS ACT
statements.title: PARENTAL RIGHTS OVER THE EDUCATION AND CARE OF THEIR KIDS ACT
sentences: Teachers would be legally required to out transgender children even if they knew that doing so would put the child at risk of physical harm or even being kicked out of their home.
Mr. Speaker, I will note that 40 percent of homeless youth are LGBTQI+ largely because they have been rejected by their families.
This bill also forbids the teaching of any subject related to the existence of transgender people.
That includes banning books, supportive student groups, or even textbooks that reference gender dysphoria.
They aren't products of a conspiracy or indoctrination.
The majority is intent on making sure that transgender kids don't have anywhere where they might feel included, recognized, or safe.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS COMMUNITY CARE SCHEDULING IMPROVEMENT ACT
statements.title: VETERANS COMMUNITY CARE SCHEDULING IMPROVEMENT ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 3482, the Veterans Community Care Scheduling Improvement Act, as amended.
One of the biggest concerns I hear from veterans is that it takes too long to get an appointment, whether at VA or through community care.

The Veterans Community Care Scheduling Improvement Act, as amended, is a solid step forward toward fixing issues that have plagued the Veterans Health Administration since before the Phoenix wait-time scandal in 2014.

The system authorized by H.R. 3482 would leverage technology to allow VA schedulers to see community care providers' schedules and book appointments directly into them, streamlining the process and allowing them to get booked days or weeks faster.
The bill also requires that VA use this technology to view VA's direct care appointments as well as the community care, giving veterans an apples-to-apples comparison of first available appointments.

While I believe that the system authorized by this act could have a substantial impact on veterans' access to timely care, I am concerned that it will only be as good as VA's ability to recruit community care providers to participate.
I think there should be more requirements in the VA's community care network contracts to mandate community provider participation.
The VA must also ensure that there is buy- in from all levels of the organization because technology is only as good as its implementation and adoption.
Mr. Speaker, I encourage my colleagues to vote ``yes'' on H.R. 3482, the Veterans Community Care Scheduling Improvement Act, as amended, and I yield back the balance of my time.
I thank Representative Barrett and Representative Budzinski for their work on this bill, and I urge my colleagues to support it.

statements.title: ESTABLISHMENT OF QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE APPOINTMENT OF A PERSON AS A MARRIAGE AND FAMILY THERAPIST, QUALIFIED TO PROVIDE CLINICAL SUPERVISION, IN THE VETERANS HEALTH ADMINISTRATION

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NO WRONG DOOR FOR VETERANS ACT

sentences: This bill would reauthorize the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program, or Fox grants, for fiscal year 2026.
As the ranking member of the Veterans' Affairs Committee, one of my top priorities has been and will continue to be veteran suicide prevention.
Community-based programs are a crucial part of a public health approach to suicide prevention.
This bill would also compound this issue by requiring grantees to use the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale to screen participants for their baseline mental health when entering the program.

While this scale is a widely accepted, clinically validated behavioral health screening instrument, its primary use is to measure a patient's suicidal ideation and the severity of suicidal risk at a given point in time.
Each of these tools measures other upstream factors of mental health that contribute to veterans' suicide risks, such as levels of emotion, optimism, work satisfaction, and social support.

Limiting grantees to the use of a single screening instrument that measures suicide risk at a point in time will further limit our ability to evaluate the overall effectiveness of the Fox grant program on improving veterans' mental health.
It was never intended to directly provide clinical care, particularly mental health care.

That said, while I have serious concerns about how this bill would reauthorize the program, I want to make clear that I understand that this grant program is a critical piece of VA's efforts in ensuring veterans receive the outreach, support, and services they need and deserve when it comes to their mental health.
Veterans deserve our best legislative efforts, not legislation that creates more problems than it solves and that does not take steps to improve suicide prevention efforts.

That being said, I will not stand in the way of forward progress on veteran suicide prevention efforts, but I strongly urge my House and Senate colleagues to work with us to ensure that final reauthorization of this program is as robust as possible.
Specifically, we oppose language that would add ``healthcare providers'' as eligible grantees.
I will always be supportive of efforts to prevent veteran suicide, but I remain concerned that this bill does not do enough to ensure the Fox Grant Program is working as intended.

I strongly support this bipartisan bill as it would promote those actors who are doing claims preparation and processing the right way, not the ones who pay to be the first result on an internet search.
Mr. Speaker, today, I urge my colleagues to support H.R. 1578 and not just to stop there.

I also urge them to continue to push back against claim sharks and to support legislation that reinstates the penalties that were in place to hold accountable bad actors who took advantage of veterans for years.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STOP TRUMP'S CHAOS--STAND UP FOR SCIENCE
statements.title: STOP TRUMP'S CHAOS--STAND UP FOR SCIENCE
sentences: They are doing remarkable work on everything from climate change to biomedical engineering.
While all of this is happening, China is investing billions in biotech, AI, and clean energy.
We are losing because we are allowing our government to sabotage them.
Madam Speaker, I represent a region full of young people who believe they can cure disease, fight climate change, and explore the stars.
Do we stand by our veterans mid-treatment, or do we tell them to wait until the budget looks better?
Madam Speaker, I urge my colleagues to reject these cuts, reject this anti-science, anti-veteran agenda.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICIES
statements.title: TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICIES
sentences: The Supreme Court unanimously ruled that the administration must facilitate the return of one such man, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Maryland father, but the executive branch has ignored the highest Court in the land, saying that their own views matter more.

I want to take the opportunity to draw attention to another case that has captured the public conscience, that of Andry Jose Hernandez Romero, a 31-year-old gay Venezuelan makeup artist and asylum seeker who was forcibly disappeared without due process.
He passed an initial asylum screening and had no criminal record.
Nobody should be disappeared out of our country without habeas corpus hearings.
Mr. Speaker, the sign behind me says ``9-0.'' ``9-0'' is the order of the Supreme Court.
This 9-0 Supreme Court order is being defied by the President.
No one in our country, no person, no man, is above the law.
We cannot permit a President to defy a 9-0 order of the Supreme Court.
No person and no man is above the law.
It strikes me that we are witnessing this evolution of this administration's policies that began with: We are just going to deport criminals.
Mr. Speaker, I remind my colleagues that, in this country, under our Constitution, no one is above the law, not even the President.
Our President, at this very moment, is defying a 9-0 Supreme Court decision.
From the very beginning, when he crossed the border, he was in custody.
He arrived with papers that show, from his native Venezuela, that he has no criminal record.
My understanding not only was that he was seeking asylum from Venezuela because of his sexual orientation but also because he would not comply with the authoritarian regime there.

Mr. Speaker, I thank Mr. Garcia for traveling to El Salvador on his own resources and to our colleagues who spent their own resources because this House of Representatives will not do oversight over the overreach of this administration, will not do oversight over the dereliction of constitutional responsibility of this administration, an administration that was defying a 9-0 Supreme Court order to facilitate the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia.
We have now seen, in just recent days, that we have moved from noncitizens to citizens being sent out of this country.

They are evidence of a pattern, a government operating outside the law, outside the Constitution, outside the decision of a Supreme Court that has ruled 9-0 that this administration must facilitate the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a government that believes that it can disappear people without charges, ignore the judiciary, and turn the Constitution into a suggestion rather than a safeguard.
Mr. Speaker, I will now move on and yield to the gentlewoman from Oregon (Ms. Hoyle).

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS EDUCATION TRANSPARENCY AND TRAINING ACT
statements.title: VETERANS EDUCATION TRANSPARENCY AND TRAINING ACT
sentences: These Shopping Sheets give student veterans more information about the schools they are considering before they take the major step of enrollment.

The Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act, authored by Representative Mike Levin, created these Shopping Sheets, benefiting student veterans around the country who now know more about what a school offers and charges.
This is a welcome improvement that ensures we won't waste time on paperwork that doesn't benefit student veterans.
Mr. Speaker, I support H.R. 981 and urge my colleagues to do the same.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MONTGOMERY GI BILL SELECTED RESERVES TUITION FAIRNESS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: MONTGOMERY GI BILL SELECTED RESERVES TUITION FAIRNESS ACT OF 2025
sentences: This program was designed to prevent foreclosures for veterans with VA home loans who had exhausted every other option.

The decision came down just hours after the new Trump tariffs sent our economy reeling, plunging the stock market, increasing job insecurity, and deepening financial strain on working families, including veterans.
They did it while Republicans in Congress are pushing massive tax cuts for millionaires and billionaires.
The Republicans are pushing for massive tax cuts for billionaires while forcing veterans into foreclosures.

That is why I am introducing the Foreclosure Assistance Immediately Reinstated, or FAIR Act, to reinstate the VASP program and make it clear that VA's job is to help veterans stay in their homes, not push them into homelessness.
VA had the tools, and has the responsibility, to intervene when veterans faced foreclosure.
I hope we finish this work in this Congress, and I urge my colleagues to support it.
Mr. Speaker, while the House debates various veterans-related legislation today, none are more urgent than the legislation I am introducing to stop thousands of veterans from losing their homes.
I urge my colleagues to support the FAIR Act and send a clear message: We don't let veterans fall through the cracks.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VIETNAM VETERANS LIVER FLUKE CANCER STUDY ACT
statements.title: VIETNAM VETERANS LIVER FLUKE CANCER STUDY ACT
sentences: I will support this bill today, but I urge my colleagues to consider that implementation of this bill will be harder than it needs to be in the new CDC workforce realities that we are now in.

In addition, while I support the underlying goals of this measure, I must express concern over the majority's decision to offset its cost by diverting pension payments from some of the VA's oldest and sickest veterans.
Mr. Speaker, with those caveats I have identified, I support this legislation, and I ask my colleagues to do the same.

statements.title: FULL-YEAR CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in opposition to this partisan Republican spending bill because it guts the Honoring our PACT Act and abandons veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxins.
Mr. Speaker, I stand with our veterans.
I stand firm in our priorities and promises, and I will not stand by while Republicans rip them apart.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on this partisan Republican spending bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONCURRENT RESOLUTION ON THE BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025
statements.title: CONCURRENT RESOLUTION ON THE BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025
sentences: Let's be clear: This is a tax break for billionaires like Elon Musk paid for by working people, including millions of our veterans.
The Republican rip-off cuts at least $880 billion from Medicaid, the program that 80 million Americans, including 9 million veterans, rely on for health insurance coverage.
This is completely unacceptable, and I urge every Member to oppose this abomination of a resolution that uses veterans as a piggy bank to pay for a billionaire tax break.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ADDRESSING THE HACK OF U.S. TREASURY PAYMENT SYSTEMS
statements.title: ADDRESSING THE HACK OF U.S. TREASURY PAYMENT SYSTEMS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, if you were approached on the street by a stranger and asked for your Social Security number, your home address, or your bank account information, you would say no.
When the government asks for this information in order to process Social Security checks or a refund, Americans say yes because there is an expectation of privacy and trust.
I was quick to cosponsor the Taxpayer Data Protection Act to protect the Nation's payment system from reckless and unlawful interference.
I will note that The New York Times reports that Elon Musk will make no public disclosure of any conflicts of interest in his financial disclosure.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
statements.title: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
sentences: We have seen an unelected billionaire attempt to lay off, fire, and purge Federal employees from across the executive branch.
He put an end to that mission in the fervor to get rid of diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts in Federal agencies.
Yes, diversity, equity, and inclusion include veterans with visual, hearing, mobility, and cognitive impairments.
These are 700 opportunities to increase veterans' access to care that will instead stay unfilled.
